mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine typically costs £850-£1,600 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. 9HV 90hp units start around £850, 9HY 109hp units from £900, 9HZ 110hp units from £950, and 9HR 112hp units from £1,000. Used engines start from £550. Supply & fit adds £400-£800 labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi (DV6) engine problems are turbocharger failure due to oil starvation (reported as early as 40,000 miles), injector seal leaks and sticking (especially on 110hp and 112hp variants), EGR valve clogging and DPF blockage from short-journey driving. The 1.6 HDi's reliability is considered mixed, with recurrent failures on several components.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £850-£1,600 versus £1,500-£5,000 for a comparable used 308. With dealer replacement potentially exceeding £4,500, specialist rebuilt units offer significant savings. The 1.6 HDi's strong fuel economy (50+ mpg) makes it a desirable engine for high-mileage drivers.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi (DV6) engine typically reaches 150,000-200,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct 5W-30 or 5W-40 specification, DPF-friendly driving (regular motorway runs) and EGR system maintenance are essential for longevity. The 1.6 HDi runs hot - sludge buildup is the primary killer of turbos and bearings.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi and 1.6 BlueHDi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 HDi (DV6) is a Euro 5 diesel fitted to first-generation 308s (2007-2013), producing 90-112hp without AdBlue. The 1.6 BlueHDi (DV5) is a Euro 6 diesel fitted to second-generation 308s (2013-2021), featuring AdBlue (SCR) for lower NOx emissions and producing 99-120hp. The BlueHDi has more complex emissions hardware and is generally more fuel-efficient but more sensitive to AdBlue system faults. The HDi is simpler and cheaper to maintain but has its own turbo and injector vulnerabilities.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine code appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Common codes include 9HV (90hp), 9HY (109hp), 9HZ (110hp) and 9HR (112hp). Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi was the dominant diesel engine across the first-generation (Phase 1, 2007-2013) 308 range, powering everything from entry-level Access to high-spec Feline trims. Part of PSA's DV6 engine family, the 1.6 HDi delivered strong fuel economy and torque - making it the backbone of UK 308 diesel sales. Available in 90hp, 110hp and 112hp outputs, the 1.6 HDi was fitted to Active, Allure, Sport, GT and Feline variants. However, its turbocharger, injector and EGR system vulnerabilities have made it a significant source of replacement enquiries for high-mileage examples. The 1.6 HDi was later replaced by the 1.6 BlueHDi (DV5) in the second-generation (Phase 2, 2013-2021) 308.

milestones.description: **2007** - First-generation 308 launched with 1.6 HDi 90hp (9HV) and 1.6 HDi 110hp (9HZ) diesel engines
**2008** - 1.6 HDi 90hp and 110hp carry over with minor ECU refinements; 9HY 109hp variant introduced for SW models
**2009** - 9HR 112hp variant introduced for GT and Feline trims
**2010** - Revised EGR and DPF calibration to improve regeneration efficiency
**2011** - Minor emissions updates ahead of Euro 5 compliance
**2012** - Final Phase 1 production; 1.6 HDi continues through to 2013
**2013** - Phase 2 (EMP2 platform) launched; 1.6 HDi replaced by 1.6 BlueHDi (DV5) and 1.5 BlueHDi (EH5)
**2014** - 1.6 HDi officially discontinued in the 308 range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 9HV, 9HY, 9HZ and 9HR engine fitted to the Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi (DV6) is the most common diesel engine in the first-generation 308, but its reliability is considered mixed - with recurrent failures on several components. Turbocharger failure, injector seal leaks and EGR clogging are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The 110hp and 112hp variants are particularly susceptible. Every rebuilt Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - Why Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi Engines Lose Boost and Smoke Excessively
problems.rootCause: The 1.6 HDi runs hot, causing sludge in the oil which can clog the turbo oil feed filter - leading to oil starvation and bearing failure. The 110hp 9HZ and 112hp 9HR variants are particularly susceptible. Symptoms include loss of power, excessive smoke, whistling noise and, in severe cases, complete turbo seizure. Turbocharger failures have been reported as early as 40,000 km.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbocharger, clean oil feed, flush oil system, replace oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if engine internals undamaged; risk of repeat failure if oil sludge not fully addressed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded turbo, oil system flush, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if turbo debris entered sump or engine shows low compression

problems.recommendation: Turbo failure on the Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi is often a symptom of wider oil circulation issues. If your engine is showing turbo symptoms, get a compression test first. If compression is good, a specialist turbo replacement with a full oil system flush may suffice. If not, a rebuilt DV6 engine with upgraded oil feed components is the smarter investment. The 1.6 HDi runs hot - regular oil changes with correct 5W-30 or 5W-40 specification are critical to preventing sludge buildup.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 9HZ/9HR Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Why Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi Engines Run Rough and Lose Power
problems.rootCause: Injector seals degrade under high thermal load, allowing combustion gases to leak and carbonise around the injector seat. The 110hp 9HZ and 112hp 9HR variants are most affected, with owners reporting clattering noises and loss of power. Injector failure can also cause diesel knock and black smoke. Replacement costs £400-£650 per injector.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove, test, replace faulty injectors, code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if only one or two injectors have failed; requires Bosch-certified equipment

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new injectors and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended when multiple injectors fail or head seats are damaged

problems.recommendation: If you experience rough idle, clattering noises or loss of power after 80,000 miles, get injector coding checked first. However, if cylinder head damage is confirmed from gas leakage, a rebuilt engine is significantly cheaper than head milling plus four new injectors. The 9HZ and 9HR variants are most susceptible - early diagnosis is critical.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi injector and engine replacement

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Blockage - Why Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi Engines Trigger Anti-Pollution Faults
problems.rootCause: Short-journey driving prevents the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature, causing soot buildup that blocks exhaust flow and triggers anti-pollution warnings. The EGR valve also clogs with carbon deposits, disrupting the air-fuel mixture. Symptoms include loss of power, limp mode, black smoke and dashboard warning lights. DPF regeneration requires regular motorway driving to complete effectively.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic reset, forced DPF regeneration, EGR valve cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: Works if blockage is early-stage and sensors are functional

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF for off-car cleaning or replacement, new EGR valve
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function if substrate isn't melted or cracked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with new DPF and EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Needed if blockage caused turbo or piston damage

problems.recommendation: For a Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi used mainly for short trips, invest in regular motorway runs to allow DPF regeneration. The 1.6 HDi's DPF is sensitive to urban driving patterns - if the anti-pollution warning appears, address it promptly. A rebuilt engine is only necessary if the DPF has caused turbo or internal damage. The DV6 engine's EGR system also benefits from periodic cleaning - carbon buildup is a classic diesel vulnerability.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi engine prices with DPF solutions

problems.h4: Dual-Mass Flywheel Wear - Why Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi Engines Vibrate at Idle
problems.rootCause: The dual-mass flywheel can wear prematurely, causing vibrations at idle, juddering during gear changes and accelerated clutch wear. This has been reported on 1.6 HDi 110hp and 112hp variants, sometimes before 60,000 miles. The flywheel damping mechanism degrades over time, especially on vehicles used for stop-start urban driving.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Dual-Mass Flywheel & Clutch Kit Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove gearbox, replace dual-mass flywheel and clutch kit, bleed hydraulic system
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents further transmission damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new flywheel and clutch, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if flywheel failure has caused crankshaft or bearing damage

problems.recommendation: Dual-mass flywheel wear on the Peugeot 308 1.6 HDi is a known issue - if you notice vibrations at idle or clutch judder, have the flywheel inspected immediately. Replacing the flywheel and clutch is a significant job but far cheaper than engine replacement. A rebuilt engine is only necessary if flywheel debris has damaged the crankshaft or bearings. The 9HZ and 9HR variants are most affected - budget for this work if buying a high-mileage example.
